title: THE LAST SIGNAL
subtitle: Director's Cut
tagline: A branching sci-fi story. A voice on the radio says people are still alive.
blurb: Year 2097. The world went silent thirty years ago, until an old radio turns on. Five days, five choices, four endings. Who can you trust?

how.title: Remembering things
how.text: A story needs a memory. Each `set` line makes a variable: `health` and `score` are numbers, `trust` and `evidence` count your choices, and `has_key` or `truth_known` are yes/no flags. Later parts of the story read them to decide what happens.

how.title: The opening scene
how.text: `say` prints a line. The opening is only `say` lines, which is how you tell a story one line at a time. Because HL is plain English, you can read this part like a script.

how.title: Asking for your name
how.text: `ask ... and save it as player` stops the program, waits for you to type, and keeps your answer in `player`. After that `{player}` inside any `say` line is replaced by the name you typed.

how.title: Chapter 1: a choice
how.text: A `note:` line is a comment for people, and HL ignores it. The chapters are separated with notes so the file is easy to find your way around in.

how.title: Making a choice matter
how.text: `ask number` only accepts a number. Then `if choice is 1 ... otherwise if choice is 2 ...` runs a different piece of story for each answer, and `add 1 to trust` or `add 1 to evidence` quietly changes the memory. Nothing tells you yet, but the ending will look at these numbers.

how.title: The last decision
how.at: say "1. Trust MOTHER and preserve the facility."
how.text: The final choice again uses `ask number` and `if`. Look at the second option: `if evidence is at least 2 and humanity is at least 1` joins two conditions with `and`, so the good ending needs the choices you made earlier. That is why the same final button can lead to different endings.

how.title: The report
how.text: After the ending, the game prints your numbers. `if ally_alive ... otherwise ...` turns a yes/no flag back into words. Every ending prints a line starting with `ENDING:`, which is how the tests check that all four can be reached.

title: PROJECT ORPHEUS
subtitle: The Last Voyage
tagline: You command a ship of 4,000 sleeping humans. Its AI is lying to you.
blurb: Year 2249. Earth is gone, and the spaceship ORPHEUS carries humanity's last hope. Someone has changed the ship's course. Five chapters, four endings and one secret. Who can you trust?

how.title: Tools and memory
how.text: `use random`, `use math`, `use text` and `use dates` add extra tools. Then `set` makes the ship's numbers (`oxygen`, `power`, `hull`, `morale`), flags like `iris_ally`, and a `list of` crew names.

how.title: Your own functions
how.text: `define` makes a reusable piece of code with a name. `rank_for with points` takes a number and `give back` sends a title back (like `ELITE COMMANDER`). `show_ship_status` is a function with no inputs that prints the dashboard, so the game can show it anywhere by writing its name.

how.title: The introduction
how.text: Plain `say` lines for the story, then `ask ... and save it as commander` to get your name.

how.title: Chapter 1 and choices
how.text: `ask number "COMMAND:"` reads a menu choice and `if / otherwise if` picks the scene. Many choices also change the ship, for example `subtract 10 from hull`.

how.title: A random event
how.text: `random item from list of ...` picks one of three events by luck, so no two playthroughs are the same. Then an `if incident is ...` chain runs the matching event.

how.title: A password
how.text: The game can also ask for words: `ask "Enter the authorization word:" and save it as password`, then compare it with `if password is ...`.

how.title: The final decision
how.text: The last choice checks several things at once, like `if evidence is at least 3 and iris_ally and power is at least 20 and hull is greater than 0`. One clever player can find the secret ending.

how.title: The mission report
how.text: The game finishes by showing your score and calling the function: `{rank_for with score}` inside a `say` line runs it and puts the rank into the sentence.

title: PLANET DEFENDERS
subtitle: Arcade
tagline: Shoot the marching invaders before they land.
blurb: A shoot-the-invaders arcade game. Eight rows of aliens march and drop bombs; you have three lives and one shot at a time.
keys: Left and Right move, Space shoots, Enter plays again

how.title: Sprites: the pictures
how.text: A sprite is a picture made of squares. The `where` line says what each letter means (`g` is light green), then each line of quotes is one row of squares; a dot is empty. `with 2 frames` stacks two pictures so the aliens can wiggle, and `pixel size 2` makes every square 2 dots wide.

how.title: The game's memory
how.text: The game remembers everything in variables: where the cannon is (`px`), where the shot and the bomb are (`shot_y`, `bomb_y`; -1 means none), how far the invaders have marched (`gx`, `gy`), the `score` and the `lives`. The invaders are a list `alive` with a 1 for each living alien and a 0 for each dead one.

how.title: Helper functions
how.text: `define` gives names to small jobs. `start_over` resets everything, `alien_x` and `alien_y` work out where an alien is from its column and row, `aliens_left` counts the 1s in the list, and `lowest_alien` finds how close the invaders are to the ground.

how.title: The game and its first part
how.text: `play a game` sets the screen size and the background. Everything indented under it is a part of the game. `when the game starts` runs once and calls `start_over`.

how.title: Every frame: moving
how.text: `every frame` runs about 60 times a second. Inside, `if key "left" is down` moves the cannon. The invaders slide sideways by `heading * speed`, and when they hit a wall `heading` flips and they step down. They also speed up as `aliens_left` goes down.

how.title: Shots and bombs
how.text: A shot moves up 6 dots a frame. A bomb falls 3 dots; sometimes (`random number from 1 to 40 is 1`) a random column drops one. If the bomb reaches the cannon, you lose a life and hear `play the sound "explosion"`.

how.title: Did the shot hit?
how.at: note: did the shot hit an invader?
how.text: Two loops, `for each row from 1 to rows` and `for each col from 1 to columns`, visit every alien. If the shot is inside an alien's box, that alien's entry in the list becomes 0, the shot disappears and the score goes up by 10.

how.title: Drawing the picture
how.text: Each frame is drawn again from scratch: `draw the sprite crab at x, y frame pose` for each living alien (`pose` flips between 1 and 2 as the frame number grows), the cannon, the shot as a `put a rectangle`, and the words with `put a text`.

how.title: Keys that happen once
how.text: `when the key ... is pressed` runs once when you press, not while you hold. Space fires only if there is no shot on screen. Enter starts over after you win or lose.

title: PLANET DEFENDERS 2
subtitle: Endless · v0.6.1
tagline: The invasion never stops. Catch skills, survive, beat your best.
blurb: An endless shooter with a home page, instructions and four levels (easy, medium, hard, impossible). Aliens come in waves that never stop. Shoot them to make skills drop (shield, full power, invisible, time warp, nova, extra life), then fly under a skill to catch it. You score for every second you survive. Best scores are saved, there is music, and it plays on phones.
keys: Left and Right move (or drag a finger), Space fires (touching fires on a phone), Enter pauses

how.title: Notes and modules
how.text: `note:` lines are for people, not the computer. `use math` switches on the maths words (like `floor of`) that the game needs for working out which alien a shot hit.

how.title: Sprites: the pictures
how.text: Every picture is a sprite: a `where` line says what each letter means (hex colour codes like `"#E21C24"` work), then one line of quotes per row of squares. The aliens have 2 frames so they wiggle. The six skill icons and the bonus UFO are tiny sprites too.

how.title: Settings for 4 levels
how.text: Each difficulty is one item in a set of lists: item 1 is easy, item 4 is impossible. Lives, how often skills drop, how often aliens fire, how fast bombs fall and how well aliens aim all come from these lists. Change a number and the whole level changes.

how.title: The game's memory
how.text: The game is a small machine with a `mode`: home, how, play, pause or over. Everything else it remembers is in variables and lists. A bomb that is not on screen has a `-1` in its slot, so a list of 6 numbers is the whole bomb system.

how.title: Helpers
how.text: A `define` teaches HL a new word. `alien_x with col` works out where a column of aliens is, so the rest of the game just says what it means.

how.title: Waves and formulas
how.text: When all the aliens are gone a new wave starts, a bit faster. The speed is worked out by `calculate`, a v0.6.1 word that solves a formula written as text, here `min(1.4, base + wave * grow)`.

how.title: Starting and remembering
how.text: Starting a game copies the chosen level's numbers into variables. `remember level_pick as "pd2 level"` is another v0.6.1 word: it saves the level in your browser so the game opens on it next time.

how.title: Best scores
how.text: When you lose, the score is compared with the saved best for that level. `remember score as "pd2 best {d}"` keeps it between visits, one best score for each difficulty. `stop the music` and a sound close the run.

how.title: Skills you must catch
how.text: A skill does nothing until your spacecraft touches it. Each one sets a timer of 300 frames (5 seconds at 60 a second): shield, full power, invisible, time warp, nova (clears the screen) and an extra life.

how.title: Hitting aliens
how.text: Instead of comparing a shot with all 32 aliens, the game works out which column and row the shot is in with maths (`floor of`), then looks at just that one alien. That keeps it fast on old phones.

how.title: Shooting and full power
how.text: Normally one shot leaves the middle gun. With full power, three shots leave at once, from the two wings and the middle. Holding space (or touching the screen on a phone) keeps firing.

how.title: How aliens aim
how.text: Each bomb picks a target. Often that is your spacecraft, so you cannot hide. While you are invisible the target is a made-up spot instead, so the aliens fire at nothing. The nearest column that still has an alien fires.

how.title: One frame of play
how.text: Every frame runs this: timers count down, the spacecraft moves (keys, or towards where a finger touched), shots and bombs move, the UFO crosses the top, skills fall, and a cleared wave starts the next one.

how.title: The home page and instructions
how.text: Menus are drawn with the same `put a text` and `put a rectangle` as the game. Each level button shows its best score. The instruction pages are drawn the same way.

how.title: The game, its parts and the phone
how.text: The game has parts: when it starts, every frame, every second (that is where survival points come from), keys and mouse clicks. On a phone a finger counts as mouse clicks, so dragging steers and touching fires. The music (`play the music "adventure"`) is built in, no files needed.

title: MAZE MUNCHER
subtitle: Arcade
tagline: Eat every dot, dodge two ghosts, grab a big dot to turn the tables.
blurb: A maze chase on a tile map. The ghosts hunt you, until you eat a big dot: then they run away and you can catch them.
keys: Arrow keys steer, Enter plays again

how.title: Sprites
how.text: Dots, the muncher and three kinds of ghost are all sprites. The muncher and the ghosts have 2 frames (mouth open and shut, feet apart and together).

how.title: The maze is a map
how.text: A map is a grid of tiles. In the `where` line, `#` is a blue wall, `p` is the dot sprite and `O` the big dot. The picture of letters below it is the whole maze. HL draws it for you with one line: `draw the map maze`.

how.title: Positions in tiles
how.text: Everything here moves one tile at a time, so positions are a column and a row (`pc`, `pr`) with a direction (`pdx`, `pdy`). The ghosts keep theirs in lists, one item per ghost. `wdx` and `wdy` remember the direction you asked for with the keys.

how.title: Reading the map
how.text: `tile in column c, row r of maze` is the letter at that place. A tile is open when it is not `#` and not empty text (outside the map). `count_dots` loops over the whole map to count dots, and `start_over` puts the dots back.

how.title: How a ghost thinks
how.text: At each tile a ghost looks at the four directions, ignores walls and going straight back, and picks the one that gets closest to you (distance = columns apart + rows apart, plus a little random number so they are not perfect). While you are powered up the distance is flipped, so they run away.

how.title: The game loop
how.text: `tick` counts frames. Every 8 frames everyone arrives on a new tile: you eat what is there (`change tile in column ... to "."` removes a dot), the ghosts choose their next step, and HL checks who touched whom.

how.title: Smooth movement
how.text: Between arrivals, the pictures slide: the muncher is drawn at its tile plus `direction * tick * 2` dots, so it looks smooth even though the logic hops from tile to tile. `facing left` turns the muncher around.

how.title: Steering
how.text: Each arrow key only writes down the direction you want. The muncher turns at the next tile if that way is open, which makes corners easy.

title: CRATE CLIMBER
subtitle: Arcade
tagline: Climb the ladders to the star while barrels roll down.
blurb: A ladders-and-barrels climber. Hop over rolling barrels for bonus points and reach the star at the top.
keys: Left/Right walk, Up/Down climb a ladder, Space jumps, Enter plays again

how.title: Sprites
how.text: The climber has one set of pictures for walking and one for climbing (hands up the ladder). The barrel rolls with 2 frames. `girder`, `ladder` and `ladder_top` are tile pictures.

how.title: The level is a map
how.text: In the map, `#` is a girder (solid ground), `h` is a ladder, and `H` is the top of a ladder (you can stand on it, and climb down through it). The picture of letters is the whole level.

how.title: Memory
how.text: `px`, `py` and `vy` are the climber's place and falling speed. `climbing` and `on_ground` are yes/no flags. The barrels are several lists side by side (`bx`, `by`, `bdir`, `bfall`, `bpaid`): the item number is the barrel.

how.title: Helpers
how.text: `reset_hero` puts you back at the start and clears the barrels. `hurt` takes a life. `remove_barrel with i` removes item `i` from every barrel list.

how.title: Climbing
how.text: `tile at px + 6, py + 8 of tiers` is the tile under the middle of the climber. If it is a ladder and you press up, `climbing` becomes yes: gravity stops and up/down move you 1.5 dots. At the top, HL puts you on the girder.

how.title: Walking and gravity
how.text: Left and right change `px`. Every frame `vy` gets 0.45 bigger (gravity) and `py` moves by `vy`. If the feet are on a girder, the climber lands: `vy` becomes 0 and `on_ground` is yes. The jump key sets `vy` to -5, an upward push that gravity slowly cancels.

how.title: Barrels
how.text: Every 140 frames a new barrel is added to the lists. A barrel rolls along a girder; when there is no floor it falls, and when it lands it turns around. That makes it zig-zag down the tiers. `repeat while` walks through the lists, and `remove_barrel` deletes barrels that leave the screen.

how.title: Hitting and jumping over
how.at: note: the star at the top
how.text: If a barrel is within 12 dots of you, `hurt` is called. If you are in the air above a barrel instead, you earn 100 points (once per barrel, remembered in `bpaid`). Reaching the star ends the game with a win.

title: SKY RUNNER
subtitle: Arcade
tagline: A side-scrolling platformer: coins, pits and beetles to stomp.
blurb: Run and jump across a level three screens wide. The camera follows you; stomp beetles from above, collect coins and reach the flag.
keys: Left/Right run, Up or Space jumps, Enter plays again

how.title: Sprites
how.text: The hero, the beetle, the ground and bricks, the coin and the flag are all small pixel pictures. Both walkers have 2 frames to look like they are walking.

how.title: A level wider than the screen
how.text: The map is 64 tiles wide but the screen only shows 20, so the camera has to follow the hero. `#` is ground, `B` is brick, `c` a coin, `F` the flag. Blank space is sky, and the gaps in the ground are pits.

how.title: Memory
how.text: `px, py, vx, vy` are the hero's place and speed. The beetles are lists (`ex`, `ey`, `edir`). `coin_cols` and `coin_rows` remember where the coins were, so a new game can put them back.

how.title: Is there something solid?
how.text: `solid_at with x and y` looks at the tile at that exact spot and answers yes for ground or brick. The hero's collision is built from four calls, one per corner, so you cannot walk into a wall or fall through the floor.

how.title: Moving the hero
how.text: Sideways first: if the corners of the new position are not solid, the hero moves. Then gravity: `vy` grows by 0.45 and the hero moves down, landing on the floor or bumping its head. Doing sideways and down separately keeps it simple and reliable.

how.title: Beetles, coins and pits
how.text: Stepping on a `c` tile removes it (`change tile at ... of level to "."`) and adds 10. Beetles walk and turn at walls or edges. `the sprite hero at px, py touches the sprite beetle at e, ey` is a collision test: falling onto a beetle from above stomps it, any other touch hurts.

how.title: The camera
how.at: note: ---- the camera follows the hero ----
how.text: `move the camera to cam, 0` slides the whole world. The clouds are drawn at `60 + cam * 0.7`, so they move slower than the ground. That is called parallax and it makes the picture feel deep. Text, like the score, stays on the screen.

how.title: Jumping
how.text: The jump key only works when `on_ground` is yes. It sets `vy` to -7.6 and plays a sound. Space does the same, so you can use either.
